items.title: Marie Curie processed tonnes of pitchblende in a leaky shed
items.claim: In 1898 Marie and Pierre Curie noticed that pitchblende (uranium ore) was more radioactive than its uranium content alone could explain. Over four years they processed tonnes of pitchblende in a leaky Paris shed and isolated two new radioactive elements: polonium (named for Marie's native Poland) and radium.
items.prompt: Why was such heroic processing required?

options.text: Polonium and radium occur at incredibly low concentrations in pitchblende — about 0.1 g of radium per tonne of ore; isolating any usable amount required chemically processing tonnes of material with manual techniques
The Curies did not have a chemistry degree

items.reveal_title: Four years, tonnes of ore, two new elements
items.reveal:
Marie Curie used a sensitive electrometer (built by Pierre and his brother Jacques) to track radioactivity in chemical fractions. She separated and refractionated until concentrated radium and polonium emerged.

The shed had a leaky roof. They worked through Paris winters. By 1902 she had isolated about 0.1 gram of radium chloride.

She won two Nobels — Physics 1903 (with Pierre and Becquerel) and Chemistry 1911 (alone, for the isolation). She is still the only person to have won Nobel prizes in two different sciences.

She died in 1934 of aplastic anaemia, almost certainly from decades of radiation exposure. Her notebooks are still so radioactive they are stored in lead-lined boxes; readers must wear protective equipment.
items.why: Some discoveries depend on raw labour with primitive equipment. The Curies isolated two elements without a research budget.

items.title: Gold is yellow because its electrons move at over half the speed of light
items.claim: Silver, copper and gold all sit in Group 11. Silver is shiny white, copper reddish, gold yellow. Gold's colour is a direct consequence of special relativity acting on its inner electrons.

options.text: Gold's 1s electrons move at about 58 percent the speed of light; relativistic mass increase contracts the 6s orbital and shrinks the 5d-to-6s gap into the visible — blue is absorbed, yellow is reflected
Gold's surface oxidises to a yellow film
Gold absorbs longer wavelengths because it is denser

items.reveal:
For silver (Z=47) the analogous d-to-s transitions sit in the ultraviolet; silver reflects all visible light evenly. For gold (Z=79) the energy gap collapses into the visible blue and absorbs around 470 nm. The complementary colour — yellow — is what bounces back at your eye.

The same relativistic 6s contraction weakens metallic bonding in mercury (Z=80), giving it a melting point of -39°C and making it the only metal liquid at room temperature.

Without special relativity, gold would be silvery white and mercury would be a solid metal like cadmium above it.
items.why: Colour is treated as an unchanging elemental property. For heavy elements it depends on relativistic effects on inner electrons.

items.title: Carbon monoxide's dipole points the wrong way
items.claim: Oxygen is more electronegative than carbon (3.44 versus 2.55). You would expect carbon monoxide to have a dipole with the negative end on oxygen. In fact the negative end sits on carbon.
items.prompt: Why does CO's dipole point from O (positive) to C (negative)?

options.text: Electronegativity values are wrong for small molecules
Oxygen donates a lone pair into a bonding orbital concentrated on carbon — the dative pi back-bonding cancels and reverses the simple electronegativity dipole
Carbon monoxide has no dipole at all
The molecule rotates so fast the dipole averages to zero

items.reveal_title: Molecular orbital theory beats Pauling's electronegativity table
items.reveal:
Drawing CO with a triple bond shows it as :C≡O: with a lone pair on each atom. But molecular orbital calculations and experiment agree: the highest occupied molecular orbital is the sigma orbital pointing AWAY from oxygen on the carbon side, giving carbon partial negative character.

This is exactly why CO is such a good ligand for transition metals — it bonds to metals through the carbon, donating that lone pair while accepting back-donation into empty pi-star orbitals. The whole of transition-metal carbonyl chemistry depends on it.
items.why: Electronegativity gives a crude bond-polarity estimate. For molecules with multiple bonds and lone pairs, the orbital picture matters more.
